title: Simultaneous transcendental element at finitely many prime fibres
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring, let $\mathfrak p_1,\ldots,\mathfrak p_r$ be prime ideals (prime ideals are proper ideals whose quotient is an integral domain) of $B$ such that no $\mathfrak p_i$ is contained in another for $i\ne j$, let $k_i$ be a subfield of the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$ [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension], and assume each extension $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)/k_i$ is not algebraic [def-weil-algebraic-element]. If $J\subset B$ is an ideal not contained in any $\mathfrak p_i$, then there exists $x\in J$ whose image in $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$ is transcendental over $k_i$ for every $i$ (the assertion is vacuous when $r=0).

proof.text: If $r=0$, take $x=0\in J$; the indexed conclusion is empty. Assume $r>0$. For each $i$ put $J_i=J\mathfrak p_1\cdots\widehat{\mathfrak p_i}\cdots\mathfrak p_r$. This ideal is not contained in $\mathfrak p_i$: choose $a\in J\setminus\mathfrak p_i$, and for each $j\ne i$ choose $b_j\in\mathfrak p_j\setminus\mathfrak p_i$, possible by the hypothesis that no two primes contain one another. The product $a\prod_{j\ne i}b_j$ lies in $J_i$ and is outside $\mathfrak p_i$, since a prime containing a finite product contains one factor. (For $r=1$ the empty product is $1$.)

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 0GTE, proof lines 8577–8581, with Algebra Lemma Tag 07K1 (product of ideals in a prime)

proof.text:
Fix $i$. For the affine scheme $\operatorname{Spec}(B)$ and the prime $\mathfrak p_i$, the local ring is $B_{\mathfrak p_i}$ and its residue field is $B_{\mathfrak p_i}/\mathfrak p_iB_{\mathfrak p_i}$. Writing $S=(B/\mathfrak p_i)\setminus\{0\}$, localization commutes with this quotient, so this quotient is $S^{-1}(B/\mathfrak p_i)=\operatorname{Frac}(B/\mathfrak p_i)$; this is the affine residue-field definition [def-weil-residue-field]. Choose a transcendental $\xi_i\in\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$, which exists because $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)/k_i$ is not algebraic. Write $\xi_i=u/v$ with $u\in B$ and $v
otin\mathfrak p_i$. Since $J_i
ot\subseteq\mathfrak p_i$, choose $c\in J_i\setminus\mathfrak p_i$ and rewrite $\xi_i=(uc)/(vc)$. Then $a_i=uc$ and $b_i=vc$ belong to $J_i$, while $b_i
otin\mathfrak p_i$ because $\mathfrak p_i$ is prime. If both images of $a_i$ and $b_i$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$ were algebraic over $k_i$, their quotient would be algebraic over $k_i$ (the algebraic elements in a field extension form a subfield), contradicting the transcendence of $\xi_i$. Thus one of $a_i,b_i$ has transcendental image; choose $x_i$ to be that element. This gives $x_i\in J_i$ with transcendental image over $k_i.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma Tag 0GTE, proof lines 8582–8587

proof.text: Set $x=x_1+\cdots+x_r$. Since each $x_i\in J_i\subseteq J$, we have $x\in J$. For a fixed $i$, every $x_j$ with $j\ne i$ lies in $\mathfrak p_i$ because $J_j$ contains the factor $\mathfrak p_i$; hence the image of $x$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$ equals the image of $x_i$, which is transcendental over $k_i$. Therefore this single $x$ has the required property at all the prime ideals.
